extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, parties, and counsel participating in AIA/PTAB proceedings (petitioners, patent owners, patent agents, and attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed amendments to 37 CFR part 42 governing trial practice before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (AIA proceedings), including filing requirements, word-count limits, evidentiary and procedural rules, sanctions, and claim construction standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of candor; signing papers; representations to the Board; sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties and individuals involved in the proceeding have a duty of candor and good faith to the Office. Every petition, response, written motion, and other paper filed must be signed by lead counsel or designated backup counsel or by an unrepresented party personally. By presenting a paper, an attorney, registered practitioner, or unrepresented party certifies, after an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances, that: (1) it is not presented for any improper purpose (e.g., to harass, cause unnecessary delay, or needlessly increase cost); (2) legal contentions are warranted by existing law or a non-frivolous argument to change law; (3) factual contentions have evidentiary support; and (4) denials of factual contentions are warranted on the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board determines a violation after notice and opportunity to respond, it may impose sanctions on attorneys, practitioners, law firms, patent agents, or parties responsible. A law firm is ordinarily jointly responsible for violations by partners/associates/employees. Motions for sanctions must be separate, describe specific conduct, be authorized under § 42.20, and require pre-notice to the other party; challenged submissions must be withdrawn/corrected within 21 days or the motion may proceed; prevailing movant may recover reasonable expenses. The Board may also act on its own initiative to show cause. Sanctions must be limited to deterrence and consistent with § 42.12, and orders imposing sanctions must describe the conduct and basis. This rule does not apply to disclosures and discovery requests/responses/objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 11-type certification for all papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend § 42.11 to add a Rule 11-type certification heading and include a certification requirement for all papers filed with the Board with provision for sanctions for noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed addition titled 'signing papers; representations to the Board; sanctions' and addition of paragraphs (b)–(d) to § 42.11 implementing signature, certification, and sanctions provisions. See the signing and representations requirements and sanctions procedures in § 42.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type-volume (word count) and page limits for petitions, motions, oppositions, and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify word counts or page limits (type-volume) for petitions, motions, oppositions, and replies and identify what is excluded from the counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific limits: Petition requesting inter partes review: 14,000 words; Petition requesting post-grant review: 18,700 words; Petition requesting covered business method patent review: 18,700 words; Petition requesting derivation proceeding: 14,000 words. Motions (excluding motions to amend): 15 pages. Motions to amend: 25 pages. Replies to patent owner responses to petitions: 5,600 words. Replies to oppositions (excluding replies to oppositions to motions to amend): 5 pages. Replies to oppositions to motions to amend: 12 pages. Word counts/page limits include any statement of material facts in support but exclude table of contents, table of authorities, certificate of service or word count, exhibits, appendix, or claim listing. Patent owner preliminary responses and patent owner responses use the same word counts as the petition; oppositions follow the same page limits as corresponding motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of word count compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Any filing whose length is specified by type-volume limits must include a certification stating the number of words in the petition, motion, opposition, or reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party may rely on the word count of the word-processing system used to prepare the document. Petitions to institute must comply with word counts but may be accompanied by a motion to waive the word counts; such motion must show how waiver is in the interests of justice and append the proposed over-length filing. If a waiver is not granted, the over-length proposed petition may be expunged or returned. Any other motion to waive must be granted in advance of filing the document for which the waiver is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument demonstrative exhibits timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrative exhibits must be served and filed with respect to oral arguments on a specified timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: § 42.70(b) requires demonstrative exhibits be served at least seven business days before oral argument and filed no later than the time of oral argument. The change from five to seven business days is intended to provide additional time to resolve disputes concerning demonstratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard for unexpired patents
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims in an unexpired patent that will not expire before a final written decision is issued, the claim shall be given its broadest reasonable construction in light of the specification of the patent in which it appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments proposed to 37 CFR 42.100(b), 42.200(b), and 42.300(b). The Office will add clarifying instructions in the Office Patent Trial Practice Guide regarding how a petitioner may determine which standard to apply in the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner preliminary response may include new testimonial evidence; institution-stage treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners are not prohibited from including new testimonial evidence with a preliminary response, and such preliminary responses are subject to the same word counts as petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board's decision whether to institute an inter partes review or post-grant review will take into account a patent owner preliminary response where filed, but supporting evidence concerning disputed material facts will be viewed in the light most favorable to the petitioner for purposes of deciding whether to institute. The petitioner may seek leave to file a reply to the preliminary response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit page numbering and spacing/formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each page of an exhibit must be uniquely numbered in sequence; block quotations must be 1.5 spaced; incorporation by reference is disallowed at panel discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 42.63(d)(2)(i) requires each page of an exhibit be uniquely numbered in sequence but does not require applying a new set of unique numbers if unique numbers already exist on the document. The Office proposes using a word count for major briefing which negates any advantage for using single spacing for block quotes, and requires 1.5 spaced block quotations for readability (37 CFR 42.6(a)(2)(iii)). Incorporation by reference at a panel's discretion is declined because it may subvert page/word limits and proceedings should be self-contained in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing supplemental information from co-pending litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may file claim construction orders and other papers from co-pending litigation as supplemental information when relevant to the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may file such papers to support motions, oppositions, or replies. Parties may also seek leave to file a motion to submit supplemental information pursuant to § 42.123, but such papers must be relevant to a claim for which the trial has been instituted. Petitioners historically have included such papers with petitions; patent owners have proffered district court claim constructions with preliminary responses or patent owner responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and filing of supplemental evidence (deposition/supplemental evidence issue)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address whether cross-examination should ordinarily take place after supplemental evidence relating to direct testimony has been served rather than filed, and whether supplemental evidence should be filed as exhibits rather than only served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will adopt comments and resolve the issue but seeks further comment on whether to amend Rule 42.52(d)(2) as suggested or to amend Rule 42.64(b)(2) to require that supplemental evidence be filed (not just served). The Office solicits input on the best way to resolve the timing/filing question.

rubrics_metrics.name: No categorical limitation on number of invalidity grounds; institution discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office declines to place a limitation on the number of grounds that a petitioner may present in a petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will use word counts for major briefing to allow parties to structure arguments as they deem best (including claim charts). The Office retains discretion under 35 U.S.C. 314(a) and 324(a) whether to institute a trial and to focus the trial on grounds meeting threshold standards and reasonably decidable within statutory timeframes. Additionally, patent owners bear a duty to support affirmative factual statements with evidence—unsupported statements will be given little or no weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of privilege for communications with domestic patent agents and foreign practitioners (seeking comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office seeks comments on whether rules regarding privilege should be issued in PTAB proceedings to explicitly recognize privilege for communications between patent applicants/owners and domestic patent agents or foreign patent practitioners under the same circumstances as communications with U.S. attorneys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office previously convened roundtables and requested public comments on confidentiality issues. It invites public comment on language, scope, or other considerations for creating such a privilege, including possible amendments to 37 CFR 42.51, 42.52, 42.55, 42.62, or 42.64 to accomplish this purpose.
